solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

parts.note: to risk money on something is to bet it

explanation.surface: A gambler stakes something on a single letter of the alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek alphabet is meant: alpha comes first, so its second letter is the one wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Greek alphabet, beta follows alpha as the second character.

parts.note: a bullet is something that travels very fast

explanation.surface: A quick-moving reporter features in a news story.
explanation.definitionFit: A short official news report or announcement broadcast on radio or television.

clue.text: Nothing in wet rubbish left drier

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
rubbish as a verb means to criticise, here signalling the letters are mangled

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Wet rubbish was left behind with nothing to dry it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' rearranges WET as TWE, and O goes inside after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth used for drying oneself after a bath is a drier in the sense of something that dries.

clue.text: Beginning to skate, took a fall — slipped up

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, here the start of skate

parts.note: to take a fall is to tumble over

explanation.surface: An ice skater tripped and went down at the very start of the routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe making a mistake or tripping physically, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Playful language getting not very far — yikes!

parts.note: a tongue is a language
an inch is a short distance
eek is a cry of alarm like yikes

explanation.surface: Jokey speech that fails to get anywhere earns a startled cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Said ironically or not seriously, so jokey or teasing in tone.

clue.text: Old king, some person I met on the way up

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading the letters from the bottom
some means only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A traveller met an ancient monarch while climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: SONIM sits in 'perSON I Met' and reads upward in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Minos was a legendary ruler of ancient Crete, keeper of the Minotaur.

indicators.note: embracing means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: lambda is the Greek letter L

explanation.surface: A Greek person hugs someone during a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazilian partner dance popular around 1990.

indicators.note: remarkably hints the letters of odd are arranged in a remarkable new way

explanation.surface: An oddly strange, very ancient bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An extinct flightless bird of Mauritius, so a bird of the past.

clue.text: Cushion frequently seen under bottom of missus

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written under another follows it
in a down clue the bottom of a word is its final letter

parts.note: often means frequently

explanation.surface: A cushion keeps turning up beneath the wife's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missus' is British slang for wife; 'bottom' tempts as a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To cushion a blow is to lessen its impact, a verb synonym.

definitions.meaning: the inside story, the real facts on a matter
positioned far beneath, read literally as two words

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the information is found at the foot of the page.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated noun is slang for the true facts; split up, the words mean situated beneath.

parts.note: crackers is informal for crazy

explanation.surface: A dog named Rover goes without his Christmas crackers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rover' looks like a dog's name, but it means a wanderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer with no fixed home is a synonym for one who roves.

clue.text: Ostentation comes initially in story, looking back

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other
looking back means the word for story is read from right to left

parts.note: a tale is a story

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of comes

explanation.surface: A showy display arrives at the start of a tale told in retrospect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking back' turns TALE into ELAT; 'initially' gives C, which goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived word means brilliant show or conspicuous flair, close to showiness.

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of the novelist's name are put out of order

explanation.surface: An order to toss Jane Austen's novel aside.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse can throw its rider, removing them from the saddle.

clue.text: I agree to try and try again!

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case
again a judge hears a case

explanation.surface: Someone backs the old motto of persevering after failure.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes 'if at first you don't succeed, try, try again'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cry of approval from British parliamentary debates, signalling agreement.

indicators.note: an unfortunate turn of events suggests the letters have gone awry and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A regrettable mishap came about through someone's negligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thoughtless of others or heedless is a synonym for careless.

parts.note: char is a fish of the trout family
a whopper is a big lie

explanation.surface: A tall fish story told by somebody named Wally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wally' is British slang for a fool, as is a 'charlie', not a name here.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British informal words for a silly person.

clue.text: Seduce mate almost entirely the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way means the letters run backwards, upward in this down entry
nearly all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: Someone lures a partner into nearly going wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost entirely' cuts PARTNER to PARTNE; 'the wrong way' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure someone into a compromising position, a close synonym of trapping.

parts.note: a balti is a type of curry cooked in a wok-like pan
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A diner complains their curry has gone stone cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Baltic is British slang for freezing weather, borrowed from the chilly Baltic Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquial British usage for freezing temperatures, from the icy northern sea.

definitions.meaning: a drink or medicine that invigorates
the keynote of a musical scale

explanation.surface: A reviving memo.
explanation.definitionFit: A pick-me-up drink, and the first degree of a scale in music.

indicators.note: back tells us the word for send is written in reverse

parts.note: to remit is to send, as payment

explanation.surface: Someone decides to return a wristwatch to the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A wristwatch can be used to measure elapsed time, so is an example of such a device.

clue.text: Treasure finally found under different palm tree

indicators.note: in a down clue this piece sits below the other
different suggests the letters of palm are made into something else
finally points to the closing letter of Treasure

explanation.surface: Buried treasure is finally dug up beneath a palm tree of another kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A deciduous broadleaf tree known for its syrup and its leaf on Canada's flag.

clue.text: Hurt toe, perhaps, first in slippery bath

indicators.note: the first letter of slippery

parts.note: a tub is a bath

explanation.surface: Someone bangs a toe stepping into a slippery bath.
explanation.definitionFit: To stub is to knock a toe against something; toe marks it as an example.

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A plain statement that something is in truth a lengthy claw.
explanation.definitionFit: The sharp hooked nail of a bird of prey is a synonym for a claw.

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-husband
ample means large or plentiful

explanation.surface: Something used to be a big suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: A case in point is an instance, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Muscular men mostly backed fee being revised

indicators.note: revising something rewrites it, so the letters are reworked
mostly means all but the last letter of backed is used

explanation.surface: A payment that was supported is being reconsidered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims BACKED to BACKE; 'being revised' rearranges it with FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for brawny, attractive men displayed for their physique.

definitions.meaning: to put up with or endure
a large furry animal such as a grizzly

explanation.surface: Put up with an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb sense means endure; the noun names a large wild mammal.
